// dryRunTimeoutMinutes: Stryker runs the whole suite once, instrumented, before it throws a single mutant, and its default ceiling for that is FIVE MINUTES. Measured 2026-09-14 on an idle 8-core machine: 1266 tests in 4 minutes and 57 seconds. Three seconds of margin is not a margin — the run had already failed twice here and the nightly had been red for two days, each time with `Initial test run timed out` and no report to read. This number is a CEILING and not a budget: what it guards against is a runner that has hung, and that does not care whether the value is 12 or 20, while a runner with half these cores does. It is declared rather than defaulted so that the reason stands beside it, and point 1 of `check-mutation` refuses the default.
// ignorePatterns: Stryker copies the repository into a sandbox and walks it ITSELF, not the git index: without this list it saw 3907 files where git knows 708. The excess is generated directories, and those have concurrent writers — `nx affected` runs `build` beside `mutation`, ng-packagr creates and deletes `tmp/libs/components/build/tsconfig.generated.<uuid>.json`, and Stryker falls over on `ENOENT ... copyfile` halfway through copying. The symptom is misleading at that: the task is flaky and passes on its own, so the first suspect was the mutant timeout. In passing, the sandbox stops copying its own previous sandboxes from `tmp/stryker`. The agent directories are here for a second reason and not for their size: two of them hold SYMLINKS to a tree in a third, and `copyFile` on a link to a directory is `EISDIR` — the run ends before the first mutant. Taking those trees out of the git index did not help and could not, because Stryker walks the WORKING TREE: what git no longer tracks is still on disk, and this list is the only place that can say so.
